title: Cygnus Loop
caption: Part of the Cygnus Loop supernova remnant, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Cygnus Loop, NGC 6960, SNR 074.0-08.5 · about 1500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: J.J. Hester (Arizona State University), and NASA

recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Hubble image archive. No published rating.

story: This Hubble image shows a small portion of the Cygnus Loop, the remains of a colossal stellar explosion. It was taken with Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera.

The Cygnus Loop traces the rim of a bubble-shaped blast wave that is still expanding outward from a star that exploded about 15,000 years ago. A supernova hurls the outer layers of a star into space, and as that material and the shock wave in front of it plough into surrounding gas, they heat it and make it glow.

Seeing only a small section of the remnant is useful. Zooming in on the edge of the blast wave lets astronomers look closely at the boundary where the explosion meets the gas between the stars, and study how the shock is moving through it. The blast wave caught in this frame is still expanding, so the scene is slowly changing.
scale: The source lists a distance of 1500 light years, so the light in this picture set out roughly 1,500 years ago.

understand.summary: This image was taken with Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera. The filters and colour mapping are not published.
understand.eye: A long telescope exposure gathers far more light than the eye, revealing faint structure along the blast wave.
